newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurodoc uses air transport to replace Eurostar.
newsitem.headline: Eurodoc uses air transport to replace Eurostar.

text.p: ABX, the express arm of Belgian railways, SNCB, said it had turned to air transport for shipments of its Eurodoc product which are normally carried by the Eurostar rail service.
The Eurostar service has been suspended since a fire in the Channel Tunnel earlier this week.
Eurodoc provides a "same-day" door-to-door express service with an end-to-end transit time of approximately 4 hours 30 minutes via Eurostar trains operating between Brussels, Paris and London.
Eurodoc shipments have an average unit weight of around 2.5 kilos.

Contingency plans for Eurodoc had centred on the use of scheduled passenger services between Antwerp city airport and London City airport, between London-City and Brussels and between London and Paris/Charles de Gaulle, Eurodoc general manager Lars Olesen, told Reuters.

"It's not been too big a logistics exercise putting temporary back-up measures in place. Admittedly, transit times are longer which means there is a possibility of early morning pick-ups only being delivered during the afternoon and afternoon pick-ups the following morning. However, the message we want to get across is that the Eurodoc service is still very much open for business trains despite the cancellation of Eurostar trains."

Olesen said that while there had been a slight fall off in traffic from Brussels since Eurostar had been withdrawn, there had been no noticeable change in the usual volume of from London to Brussels. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017.
